text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a common practice in modern software development. When developers write new code, they regularly add it to a shared project. Each time this happens, an automated build starts. This means the system checks that the code works and combines it with the existing project. The CI pipeline also runs tests automatically. These tests help the team catch issues early, before the software is released. Finding problems quickly makes them easier and cheaper to fix. As a result, CI helps teams work faster and produce more reliable software.
